k: I know the way out from here. Go on — I'll be home before you. And don't tell Nim. I want to tell her myself.
src: 'I know the way out from here. Go on — I\'ll be home before you. And don\'t tell Nim. I want to tell her myself.'

k: We found Jorah alive in the Glass Caverns, sealed behind a wall of glass. The fork broke it like sugar. I keep thinking about that.
src: 'We found Jorah alive in the Glass Caverns, sealed behind a wall of glass. The fork broke it like sugar. I keep thinking about that.'

k: The cavern opens into a bowl of glass a hundred feet across, smooth as the inside of a bell. Bones and wreckage lie in drifts against the walls: oxen, wagons, a caravan's worth of copper pots.
src: 'The cavern opens into a bowl of glass a hundred feet across, smooth as the inside of a bell. Bones and wreckage lie in drifts against the walls: oxen, wagons, a caravan\'s worth of copper pots.'

k: In the center, the glass floor bulges. Then it _moves_.
src: 'In the center, the glass floor bulges. Then it _moves_.'

k: Is it too late to mention I'm allergic to queens?
src: 'Is it too late to mention I\'m allergic to queens?'

k: You're allergic to everything that's trying to eat us.
src: 'You\'re allergic to everything that\'s trying to eat us.'

k: It's a very common allergy.
src: 'It\'s a very common allergy.'

k: Stand together! She's— sweet Dawn, she's the size of a _street_—
src: 'Stand together! She\'s— sweet Dawn, she\'s the size of a _street_—'

k: The Sand Wyrm Queen coils, uncoils, and lies still. All through the caverns, the singing glass goes quiet — as if it had been holding a note for her, and could finally let it go.
src: 'The Sand Wyrm Queen coils, uncoils, and lies still. All through the caverns, the singing glass goes quiet — as if it had been holding a note for her, and could finally let it go.'

k: The brood will scatter now. The caravans will be safe. For a while.
src: 'The brood will scatter now. The caravans will be safe. For a while.'

k: Let's tell Oyelaran.
src: 'Let\'s tell Oyelaran.'

k: We killed the Sand Wyrm Queen in the deep caverns. When she died, all the glass stopped singing at once.
src: 'We killed the Sand Wyrm Queen in the deep caverns. When she died, all the glass stopped singing at once.'

k: Three days down out of the Greyspine. The snow becomes rain, the rain becomes fen,
src: 'Three days down out of the Greyspine. The snow becomes rain, the rain becomes fen,'

k: and nobody says very much at all.
src: 'and nobody says very much at all.'

k: So. Swamp.
src: 'So. Swamp.'

k: Fen, kid. A swamp is a fen that's let itself go.
src: 'Fen, kid. A swamp is a fen that\'s let itself go.'

k: It smells like a swamp.
src: 'It smells like a swamp.'

k: They all do.
src: 'They all do.'

k: He'd have had a word for it. Halvard. Some old monk word for "place that smells."
src: 'He\'d have had a word for it. Halvard. Some old monk word for "place that smells."'

k: I'm fine. I am entirely — I'm fine.
src: 'I\'m fine. I am entirely — I\'m fine.'

k: You are not fine. Your face is doing the thing.
src: 'You are not fine. Your face is doing the thing.'

k: What thing?
src: 'What thing?'

k: The thing Wren's face did at the Kindling. Before she cried.
src: 'The thing Wren\'s face did at the Kindling. Before she cried.'

k: I did _not_—
src: 'I did _not_—'

k: ...Okay. A little.
src: '...Okay. A little.'

k: Wren takes the case of tuning forks out of her pack. Five silver forks in blue velvet, humming faintly in the rain.
src: 'Wren takes the case of tuning forks out of her pack. Five silver forks in blue velvet, humming faintly in the rain.'

k: Halvard said they're not tuned to the Dawnsong. They're tuned to its _reflection_.
src: 'Halvard said they\'re not tuned to the Dawnsong. They\'re tuned to its _reflection_.'

k: Three things. One: the Hierophant gave you those. Two: Garrick's soldiers have been a day behind us since Saltglass. Three: Halvard is dead because of whatever they're for.
src: 'Three things. One: the Hierophant gave you those. Two: Garrick\'s soldiers have been a day behind us since Saltglass. Three: Halvard is dead because of whatever they\'re for.'

k: We don't know that.
src: 'We don\'t know that.'

k: We don't _know_ it.
src: 'We don\'t _know_ it.'

k: Here's what I know. Cassian Lorne once pulled me out of a burning troop-ship by my collar.
src: 'Here\'s what I know. Cassian Lorne once pulled me out of a burning troop-ship by my collar.'

k: And in twenty years I have never once seen that man do anything without knowing exactly why.
src: 'And in twenty years I have never once seen that man do anything without knowing exactly why.'

k: They are singing. Very quietly.
src: 'They are singing. Very quietly.'

k: The same song the Lantern sang when I stood in it. But backwards.
src: 'The same song the Lantern sang when I stood in it. But backwards.'

k: Can we chuck 'em in the swamp?
src: 'Can we chuck \'em in the swamp?'

k: ...No. We keep them. We just don't give them to anybody else.
src: '...No. We keep them. We just don\'t give them to anybody else.'

k: She shuts the case. It goes on humming.
src: 'She shuts the case. It goes on humming.'

k: Mother Osk keeps the Mirefen Lantern. If the Choir's been here—
src: 'Mother Osk keeps the Mirefen Lantern. If the Choir\'s been here—'

k: Then she needs to know what Halvard knew.
src: 'Then she needs to know what Halvard knew.'

k: And we need a roof. And soup. Halvard used to say soup was a sacrament.
src: 'And we need a roof. And soup. Halvard used to say soup was a sacrament.'

k: Was that a joke? Did the big guy just make a joke?
src: 'Was that a joke? Did the big guy just make a joke?'

k: It was a _tribute_.
src: 'It was a _tribute_.'

k: Halvard is gone. We came down out of the mountains into the fens without him. The forks are still in my pack. I can't make myself throw them away.
src: 'Halvard is gone. We came down out of the mountains into the fens without him. The forks are still in my pack. I can\'t make myself throw them away.'

k: A notice, nailed to the post. The rain has run the ink — but not enough.
src: 'A notice, nailed to the post. The rain has run the ink — but not enough.'

k: *WANTED* by order of the Lord-Commander of the Dawnguard:nA GIRL, black hair, pale, about sixteen, answers to "Sable."nTraveling with a red-haired Vanguard; a Mender; a disgraced squire; a street child; and a man who owes money.n*5,000 gold — ALIVE.*
src:
'*WANTED* by order of the Lord-Commander of the Dawnguard:
A GIRL, black hair, pale, about sixteen, answers to "Sable."
Traveling with a red-haired Vanguard; a Mender; a disgraced squire; a street child; and a man who owes money.
*5,000 gold — ALIVE.*'

k: "A street child." I've got a _name_.
src: '"A street child." I\'ve got a _name_.'

k: "A man who owes money." That's slander.
src: '"A man who owes money." That\'s slander.'

k: ...It's accurate. But it's slander.
src: '...It\'s accurate. But it\'s slander.'

k: "Disgraced squire." They didn't even spell it wrong. I'd have preferred they spelled it wrong.
src: '"Disgraced squire." They didn\'t even spell it wrong. I\'d have preferred they spelled it wrong.'

k: "Alive." He wants me alive.
src: '"Alive." He wants me alive.'

k: That's... good?
src: 'That\'s... good?'

k: I do not know. I do not know what he wants me alive _for_.
src: 'I do not know. I do not know what he wants me alive _for_.'

k: Five thousand gold. We could turn you in and steal you back.
src: 'Five thousand gold. We could turn you in and steal you back.'

k: I like how the kid thinks.
src: 'I like how the kid thinks.'

k: Dawnguard Sergeant
src: 'Dawnguard Sergeant'

k: Halt! By order of the Lord-Commander, every traveler on this causeway is to be searched for—
src: 'Halt! By order of the Lord-Commander, every traveler on this causeway is to be searched for—'

k: Black hair. Pale. That's _her_. That's the—
src: 'Black hair. Pale. That\'s _her_. That\'s the—'

k: Sergeant! Is it Sergeant? I can't tell with the helmet. Hello. We are a traveling theater troupe.
src: 'Sergeant! Is it Sergeant? I can\'t tell with the helmet. Hello. We are a traveling theater troupe.'

k: Kestrel? Bram _Kestrel_?
src: 'Kestrel? Bram _Kestrel_?'

k: Not a very _good_ theater troupe.
src: 'Not a very _good_ theater troupe.'

k: Take the girl! The rest are worth nothing!
src: 'Take the girl! The rest are worth nothing!'

k: The Lord-Commander will hear of this, Kestrel! He'll — he'll—
src: 'The Lord-Commander will hear of this, Kestrel! He\'ll — he\'ll—'

k: They knew my name.
src: 'They knew my name.'

k: Everybody knows your name, big man. You say it very loudly.
src: 'Everybody knows your name, big man. You say it very loudly.'

k: Garrick has pickets this far south. Either he's ahead of us, or he's everywhere.
src: 'Garrick has pickets this far south. Either he\'s ahead of us, or he\'s everywhere.'

k: Then we keep moving.
src: 'Then we keep moving.'

k: Word came down the water: Mother Osk's sitting up and shouting at people. Best news I've had in a month.
src: 'Word came down the water: Mother Osk\'s sitting up and shouting at people. Best news I\'ve had in a month.'

k: If you're ever back this way, my punt's yours. Free. Well. Half price.
src: 'If you\'re ever back this way, my punt\'s yours. Free. Well. Half price.'

k: Gaspar's the name, poling's the game. Was the game. Nobody's crossing the fen since the light went out.
src: 'Gaspar\'s the name, poling\'s the game. Was the game. Nobody\'s crossing the fen since the light went out.'

k: Mother Osk took the fever the very night the Choir barge came. Coincidence, the Choir said. Very sure of themselves, the Choir.
src: 'Mother Osk took the fever the very night the Choir barge came. Coincidence, the Choir said. Very sure of themselves, the Choir.'

k: The village is east. Mind the toads. They've gone strange.
src: 'The village is east. Mind the toads. They\'ve gone strange.'

k: Are you from the Cathedral? Did they send it back? Did they—
src: 'Are you from the Cathedral? Did they send it back? Did they—'

k: Oh. You're... you're children.
src: 'Oh. You\'re... you\'re children.'

k: We're carrying letters to the Keepers. From Aurenne. The Hierophant sent us.
src: 'We\'re carrying letters to the Keepers. From Aurenne. The Hierophant sent us.'

k: _The Hierophant._
src: '_The Hierophant._'

k: Then you're too late. Or too early. I don't know which.
src: 'Then you\'re too late. Or too early. I don\'t know which.'

k: Mother Osk has the rot. The black-vein fever. Doctor Vey says she won't see morning.
src: 'Mother Osk has the rot. The black-vein fever. Doctor Vey says she won\'t see morning.'

k: Where is she?
src: 'Where is she?'

k: In the Lantern. She won't let us move her. She says a Keeper dies at her light.
src: 'In the Lantern. She won\'t let us move her. She says a Keeper dies at her light.'

k: ...Even when the light's gone out.
src: '...Even when the light\'s gone out.'

k: I'm a Mender. Take me to her. Now, please.
src: 'I\'m a Mender. Take me to her. Now, please.'

k: The Lantern — north-east, past the Rot House! Hurry!
src: 'The Lantern — north-east, past the Rot House! Hurry!'

k: Well. That's the soup off.
src: 'Well. That\'s the soup off.'

k: I know. I know. Jokes are a reflex. Like flinching.
src: 'I know. I know. Jokes are a reflex. Like flinching.'

k: Mirefen. Mother Osk is dying of the Gloam-rot, and her Lantern is dark. Ilse didn't even wait to be asked.
src: 'Mirefen. Mother Osk is dying of the Gloam-rot, and her Lantern is dark. Ilse didn\'t even wait to be asked.'

k: The room smells of willow bark and fever. In the bed against the wall, under three blankets, a small old woman is shivering hard enough to rattle the frame.
src: 'The room smells of willow bark and fever. In the bed against the wall, under three blankets, a small old woman is shivering hard enough to rattle the frame.'
